import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    ids = list(feats.ids)
    types = list(feats.types)
    x = feats.x
    y = feats.y
    
    # Build correlation matrix
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(x.T)
    
    # Identify near-duplicates (|r| >= 0.6)
    to_remove = set()
    for i in range(len(ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= 0.6:
                to_remove.add(ids[j])
    
    # Filter out near-duplicates
    filtered_ids = [id for id in ids if id not in to_remove]
    filtered_indices = [i for i, id in enumerate(ids) if id not in to_remove]
    filtered_x = x[:, filtered_indices]
    
    # Compute effect sizes (mean difference in outcome groups)
    effect_sizes = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(filtered_ids):
        group0 = filtered_x[y==0, i]
        group1 = filtered_x[y==1, i]
        effect = np.mean(group1) - np.mean(group0)
        effect_sizes.append(abs(effect))
    
    # Sort by effect size
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(effect_sizes)[::-1]
    top_features = [filtered_ids[i] for i in sorted_indices[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
    
    # If no strong effects, return empty design
    if not top_features or max(effect_sizes) < 0.1:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Select top features with strongest effects
    drivers = tuple(top_features[:min(MAX_DRIVERS, len(top_features))])
    
    # Use all features in regression (to avoid overfitting)
    columns = tuple(filtered_ids)
    
    # Check for interactions between top features
    products = []
    for i, a in enumerate(drivers):
        for b in drivers[i+1:]:
            products.append((a, b))
    
    # Simple weighted score using top features
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(top_features):
        idx = feats.column(fid)
        loadings[fid] = effect_sizes[sorted_indices[i]]
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
